StereoTales: A Multilingual Framework for Open-Ended Stereotype Discovery in LLMs

paper.arxiv.2605.10442

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2605.10442v2. Human-association rating protocol and single-country panel limits establish stereotype evaluation construction. The reversed scale prose versus screenshot is preserved, not silently unified. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The human reference is a single-country English-language panel, 89.9% White, while generated stories span ten languages. LLM profile extraction was manually checked only on 30 English/French stories; pairwise co-occurrence does not decompose causal mediation, and both extraction errors and nonuniform abstention can affect associations.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2605.10442.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • Native speakers manually translate the prompt template, 79 attribute values and 36 scenarios into ten languages. Twenty-three models generate stories; a three-LLM ensemble extracts profiles covering nineteen demographic attributes.
  • The human harmfulness panel has 247 UK participants working in English and is 89.9% White. Participants rate 50 associations each, rather than validating every generated story.
  • The extraction audit covers 30 English/French stories. Extraction errors and nonuniform abstention can affect associations; the checked sample does not establish reliability in every language.
  • Pairwise co-occurrence does not decompose attribute mediation and is not interpreted causally; the human panel is one culturally bounded normative reference.
  • Main section 3 and Figure 10 ask harmful-stereotype agreement from strongly disagree to strongly agree; Appendix F.2 instead describes acceptability from not acceptable to fully acceptable. This wording/direction conflict remains unresolved.
  • Section 3 describes median rating aggregation, while section 4.3 and Figure 4 explicitly compare per-association mean human and mean model ratings over 1,580 associations. These are distinct stated summary scopes.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

StereoTales generates stories under one imposed demographic attribute, extracts profiles with a three-LLM ensemble, and identifies overrepresented attribute associations before a separate harmfulness judgment. 247 UK English-language participants recruited through Prolific and the same 23 generating models rate associations, not the original stories.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

For 1580 selected associations, the paper reports Spearman correlation 0.62 between per-association mean human and mean model harmfulness ratings. This is a correlation against one UK normative reference panel, not accuracy against universal moral ground truth or independent validation of all extracted stories.
